rounds.summary: A pre_tool hook on asb run that blocks once per round with a data-derived digest and asks for a hit ledger before spending the round.
rounds.observation: Passed the screen 2/2, then failed all 4 top-up trials (2/6). Not accepted. The critic made the proposer remove a supporting instructions note as over budget, arguably too strict.

plan.problem: The parent passes about 50% overall (P 1/3, S 2/3 in round 3). Propylene (P) is stuck at 1/3 across rounds 1, 3 and 4. Two of the propylene failures were discovery shortfalls: LGkcbM5 with 5 hits and aCihm6k with 6 hits against the 7 needed. Both ran a one-slot-per-element sweep in round 1 and only exploited in round 2 or 3. In Suzuki (S) every agent said it could not count standouts because the cutoffs are hidden. The only attempt to fix this, the round-4 "discovery ledger" instructions section, was followed literally by 1 of 6 trials, so it never had a chance to work. Hooks are the only channel with 12/12 compliance, but the parent's only hook fires after delivery, which is too late to affect discovery. I can't tell which gate failed in the other four P failures or the S failures, so this plan targets only the discovery-timing failures and the missing hit estimate.

edits.hypothesis: A once-per-round pre_tool hook on the Bash command `asb run` will make the agent state a hit ledger before it spends rounds 2 and later, and rounds 2+ will then shift toward neighbours of the best results. The hook is tools/round_gate.py, registered in hooks.json as a pre_tool entry with matcher Bash. It reads the event JSON and acts only if the command contains `asb run`. It then globs round_*_results.csv in the cwd, and passes only if there is at least one prior results file. The first time per session and per prior-round count, it exits 2. It cannot know the threshold, so its stderr message gives only numbers computed from the data. For each results file it reports the row count, the top 5 values, and how many values lie in the top 10% of all values observed so far. If the id column has structured fields, it adds one line per field level, giving the best value seen and its count. The message asks the agent to write three numbers: hits so far against the task's stated discovery target, hits still needed, and hits needed per remaining round. If the needed rate exceeds what the last round delivered, at least about 60% of the next batch should be unordered near neighbours of the best items, changing one factor at a time, plus the model's top picks. Levels whose best result is near the floor should be dropped. For group-relative targets with hidden cutoffs, use the top few percent of each group's observed values as the hit proxy. The second `asb run` attempt in the same state passes, so a rejected-then-retried request is never blocked twice and no round is lost. Falsifiable: in post-change trajectories the ledger numbers appear before rounds 2 and 3 in at least 5 of 6 trials, up from 1 of 6 under the round-4 text. P trials reach at least 7 hits in at least 2 of 3. S pass rate stays at or above the parent's 2/3. It is refuted if P stays at or below 1/3 with a shortfall below 7 hits in any failing trial despite the ledger being written, or if any S trial regresses because of over-exploitation.

plan.why_not_simpler: The simpler lever, more instruction text, was tried in round 4 and followed in 1 of 6 trials, so another paragraph is unlikely to change behaviour. Deleting the stop hook would save tokens but would not address the discovery failures. It would also drop the audit that preserved known-good models in passing trials such as k3Tgise, qEzUmRt and the passing S trials. A larger tool such as an automatic batch designer would be a rewrite, and it would encode design choices the evidence cannot yet support. This plan adds one small non-destructive nudge at the only moment that matters, just before an irreversible round is spent. The hook computes only generic descriptive numbers, so it contains no task identity, thresholds or answers.
plan.regression_risk: The risks are listed below. (1) A blocked `asb run` costs one extra step per round, and the second attempt passes. The hook must never block twice for the same state, must exit 0 on malformed input, and must exit 0 when the command is not `asb run`. It must also exit 0 when the command is a repeat of the latest accepted batch, a harmless re-run. Smoke tests must cover these cases offline. (2) Over-exploitation could hurt the held-out ranking gate by shrinking coverage. This is the largest risk. Round-4 S passes were exploit-heavy (36 of 48 in djh5T3X), so S should be fine, but the message says explicitly to keep some under-sampled coverage. (3) The agent may over-trust the top-10% proxy. +#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Once-per-round pre_tool hook on Bash: before an irreversible `asb run`, ask for a hit ledger.
+
+Reads the pre_tool event JSON on stdin. It acts only when the Bash command contains `asb run` and at least one
+earlier round_*_results.csv exists. It then summarises the results so far (descriptive numbers only, no thresholds
+of its own) and exits 2 once for that state, feeding the summary and a request back to the agent on stderr.
+The retried `asb run` in the same state passes, so no round is ever lost. Exit 0 on anything unexpected, on
+commands that are not `asb run`, and when the batch is a repeat of the latest accepted one.
+Stdlib only. Run with --selftest for a built-in check using temporary fixtures.
+"""
+import csv
+import glob
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import re
+import shlex
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+MARKER_ENV = "RSI_GATE_MARKER_DIR"
+RUN_RE = re.compile(r"\basb\s+run\b")
+ROUND_RE = re.compile(r"round_(\d+)_results\.csv$")
+SEP_RE = re.compile(r"[-_:;/ ]+")
+NUM_RE = re.compile(r"^[+-]?\d*\.?\d+$")
+MAX_LEVEL_FIELDS = 6
+MAX_LEVELS = 12
+MAX_CARDINALITY = 30
+
+
+def to_float(text):
+    try:
+        v = float(text)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return None
+    return v if math.isfinite(v) else None
+
+
+def run_args(command):
+    """Tokens following `asb run` in the command, or [] if they cannot be parsed."""
+    m = RUN_RE.search(command)
+    if not m:
+        return []
+    tail = command[m.end():]
+    tail = re.split(r"&&|\|\||;|\n", tail)[0]
+    try:
+        return shlex.split(tail)
+    except ValueError:
+        return tail.split()
+
+
+def candidate_dirs(event, command):
+    dirs = []
+    try:
+        here = os.getcwd()
+    except OSError:
+        here = None
+    for d in (event.get("cwd"), here):
+        if d and isinstance(d, str) and os.path.isdir(d):
+            dirs.append(os.path.realpath(d))
+    for m in re.finditer(r"\bcd\s+([^\s;&|]+)", command):
+        p = os.path.expanduser(m.group(1).strip("'\""))
+        if not os.path.isabs(p) and dirs:
+            p = os.path.join(dirs[0], p)
+        if os.path.isdir(p):
+            dirs.insert(0, os.path.realpath(p))
+    for tok in run_args(command):
+        if tok.startswith("-"):
+            continue
+        base = os.path.dirname(tok)
+        if base:
+            p = base if os.path.isabs(base) else os.path.join(dirs[0] if dirs else "", base)
+            if os.path.isdir(p):
+                dirs.append(os.path.realpath(p))
+    seen, out = set(), []
+    for d in dirs:
+        if d not in seen:
+            seen.add(d)
+            out.append(d)
+    return out
+
+
+def find_results(dirs):
+    """round number -> path, keeping the first directory that has each round."""
+    found = {}
+    for d in dirs:
+        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "round_*_results.csv")):
+            m = ROUND_RE.search(os.path.basename(path))
+            if m and int(m.group(1)) not in found:
+                found[int(m.group(1))] = path
+    return [found[k] for k in sorted(found)]
+
+
+def read_results(path):
+    """Return (id_column_name, [(id, value)]) using the first column as id and the last numeric column as value."""
+    try:
+        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
+            rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
+    except OSError:
+        return None, []
+    if len(rows) < 2:
+        return None, []
+    header, body = rows[0], [r for r in rows[1:] if r]
+    best_col = None
+    for col in range(len(header) - 1, 0, -1):
+        good = sum(1 for r in body if col < len(r) and to_float(r[col]) is not None)
+        if body and good >= 0.8 * len(body):
+            best_col = col
+            break
+    if best_col is None:
+        return header[0], []
+    out = []
+    for r in body:
+        v = to_float(r[best_col]) if best_col < len(r) else None
+        if v is not None:
+            out.append((r[0], v))
+    return header[0], out
+
+
+def read_ids(path):
+    try:
+        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
+            rows = list(csv.reader(fh))
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    return [r[0] for r in rows[1:] if r]
+
+
+def is_repeat(args, dirs, latest_ids):
+    """True when the batch file named in the command has exactly the ids of the latest accepted round."""
+    for tok in args:
+        if tok.startswith("-") or not tok.lower().endswith(".csv"):
+            continue
+        paths = [tok] if os.path.isabs(tok) else [os.path.join(d, tok) for d in dirs]
+        for p in paths:
+            if os.path.isfile(p):
+                ids = read_ids(p)
+                return ids is not None and bool(ids) and set(ids) == latest_ids
+        return False
+    return False
+
+
+def load_catalog(dirs, id_name):
+    """Optional join: the largest csv under <dir>/data with the id column and low-cardinality factor columns."""
+    best = None
+    for d in dirs:
+        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "data", "*.csv")):
+            try:
+                with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
+                    rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+            if rows and id_name in rows[0] and len(rows[0]) > 2 and (best is None or len(rows) > len(best)):
+                best = rows
+    if not best:
+        return {}
+    fields = []
+    for name in best[0]:
+        if name == id_name:
+            continue
+        levels = {r.get(name) for r in best}
+        if 2 <= len(levels) <= MAX_CARDINALITY:
+            fields.append(name)
+    return {r[id_name]: {f: r.get(f) for f in fields} for r in best if r.get(id_name) is not None}
+
+
+def factors_for(item_id, catalog):
+    """Map field name -> list of levels for this item, derived from the id itself or the catalog join."""
+    if item_id in catalog:
+        return {k: [v] for k, v in catalog[item_id].items() if v not in (None, "")}
+    if "|" in item_id:
+        return {"field%d" % (i + 1): [p] for i, p in enumerate(item_id.split("|"))}
+    parts = [p for p in SEP_RE.split(item_id) if p]
+    if len(parts) > 1:
+        words = [p for p in parts if not NUM_RE.match(p)]
+        if words:
+            return {"part": words}
+    return {}
+
+
+def summarise(paths, dirs):
+    per_file, allrows = [], []
+    id_name = None
+    for p in paths:
+        name, rows = read_results(p)
+        id_name = id_name or name
+        per_file.append((os.path.basename(p), rows))
+        allrows.extend(rows)
+    if not allrows:
+        return None
+    vals = sorted(v for _, v in allrows)
+    cut = vals[min(len(vals) - 1, int(math.floor(0.9 * len(vals))))]
+    lines = ["Results so far: %d items over %d round(s); top-10%% line of all observed values = %.4g."
+             % (len(allrows), len(per_file), cut)]
+    for fname, rows in per_file:
+        vs = sorted((v for _, v in rows), reverse=True)
+        top = ", ".join("%.4g" % v for v in vs[:5])
+        n_top = sum(1 for v in vs if v >= cut)
+        lines.append("  %s: %d rows, top 5 = [%s], %d at or above the top-10%% line" % (fname, len(rows), top, n_top))
+    catalog = load_catalog(dirs, id_name) if id_name else {}
+    stats = {}
+    for item_id, v in allrows:
+        for field, levels in factors_for(item_id, catalog).items():
+            for lv in set(levels):
+                n, best = stats.setdefault(field, {}).get(lv, (0, None))
+                stats[field][lv] = (n + 1, v if best is None else max(best, v))
+    shown = 0
+    for field in sorted(stats):
+        levels = {lv: nb for lv, nb in stats[field].items() if nb[0] < len(allrows)}
+        if len(levels) < 2 or len(levels) > MAX_CARDINALITY or shown >= MAX_LEVEL_FIELDS:
+            continue
+        shown += 1
+        ranked = sorted(levels.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1][1], kv[0]))[:MAX_LEVELS]
+        lines.append("  by %s (level: best value, n tried): %s" % (
+            field, "; ".join("%s: %.4g, %d" % (lv, b, n) for lv, (n, b) in ranked)))
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+MESSAGE = """Before the next irreversible round: write a short hit ledger, then re-issue the same `asb run`.
+(This check appears once per round; the retry goes through unchanged and nothing is lost.)
+
+{summary}
+
+Ledger, in your reply, with real numbers:
+ 1. Hits so far against the task's stated discovery target (use the task's own threshold or rule).
+ 2. Hits still needed, and hits needed per remaining round.
+ 3. Hits the last round actually delivered.
+If the needed rate is above what the last round delivered, lean the next batch toward unordered near neighbours of
+the best items so far (changing one factor at a time) plus the model's top picks, and drop levels whose best result
+is near the floor. Coverage of under-sampled levels matters just as much, because the held-out ranking gate needs it:
+this is guidance, not a fixed split. If the needed rate is at or below the delivered rate, keep your current split.
+If the discovery target is relative to a group whose cutoffs are hidden, count as a hit proxy the top few percent
+of each group's own observed values. The proxy is advisory and noisy; do not treat a value near a line as a hit."""
+
+
+def state_tag(paths):
+    """Hash of the contents of every results file, so the once-per-round state follows the data itself."""
+    h = hashlib.sha1()
+    for p in paths:
+        h.update(os.path.basename(p).encode("utf-8", "replace"))
+        try:
+            with open(p, "rb") as fh:
+                h.update(fh.read())
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+    return h.hexdigest()[:16]
+
+
+def marker_path(session, tag):
+    base = os.environ.get(MARKER_ENV) or os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "rsi_round_gate")
+    safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", session)[:60]
+    return base, os.path.join(base, "%s_%s.done" % (safe, tag))
+
+
+def evaluate(event):
+    """Return the message to block with, or None to let the call through."""
+    command = ""
+    ti = event.get("tool_input")
+    if isinstance(ti, dict):
+        command = str(ti.get("command") or "")
+    if not command or not RUN_RE.search(command):
+        return None
+    dirs = candidate_dirs(event, command)
+    paths = find_results(dirs)
+    if not paths:
+        return None
+    summary = summarise(paths, dirs)
+    if summary is None:
+        return None
+    _, last_rows = read_results(paths[-1])
+    if is_repeat(run_args(command), dirs, {i for i, _ in last_rows}):
+        return None
+    session = str(event.get("session_id") or "")
+    if not session:
+        return None  # no per-session key means no safe place for once-per-round state: never block
+    base, marker = marker_path(session, state_tag(paths))
+    if os.path.exists(marker):
+        return None
+    os.makedirs(base, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(marker, "w") as fh:
+        fh.write("1")
+    return MESSAGE.format(summary=summary)
+
+
+def handle(raw):
+    """(exit code, stderr text) for one raw event; anything unexpected lets the call through."""
+    try:
+        event = json.loads(raw or "{}")
+        if not isinstance(event, dict):
+            return 0, ""
+        msg = evaluate(event)
+    except Exception:
+        return 0, ""
+    return (2, msg + "\n") if msg else (0, "")
+
+
+def main():
+    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
+        return selftest()
+    code, text = handle(sys.stdin.read())
+    if text:
+        sys.stderr.write(text)
+    return code
+
+
+def selftest():
+    """In-process checks on temporary fixtures; every failure is printed to stdout with the offending output."""
+    import shutil
+    import traceback

+    tmp = None
+    old_cwd = None
+    old_marker = os.environ.get(MARKER_ENV)

+        tmp = os.path.realpath(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="roundgate_"))
+        try:
+            old_cwd = os.getcwd()
+        except OSError:
+            old_cwd = None
+        os.chdir(tmp)
+        os.environ[MARKER_ENV] = os.path.join(tmp, "m")
+        last = {"out": None}
+
+        def run(event, raw=None):
+            code, err = handle(json.dumps(event) if raw is None else raw)
+            last["out"] = (code, err)
+            return code, err
+
+        def check(name, cond):
+            print("%s %s" % ("ok  " if cond else "FAIL", name), flush=True)
+            if not cond:
+                fails.append(name)
+                print("     last result (exit code, stderr): %r" % (last["out"],), flush=True)
+
+        def ev(cmd, cwd, sid="s1"):
+            return {"hook_event_name": "PreToolUse", "tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": cmd},
+                    "cwd": cwd, "session_id": sid}
+
+        w = os.path.join(tmp, "w")
+        os.makedirs(os.path.join(w, "data"))
+        with open(os.path.join(w, "round_1_results.csv"), "w") as fh:
+            fh.write("item,score\nred_big,1.9\nred_small,1.2\nblue_big,0.5\nblue_small,1.8\n")
+        with open(os.path.join(w, "round_2.csv"), "w") as fh:
+            fh.write("item\nred_medium\nblue_medium\n")
+        with open(os.path.join(w, "round_1.csv"), "w") as fh:
+            fh.write("item\nred_big\nred_small\nblue_big\nblue_small\n")
+        cmd = "asb run round_2.csv --output round_2_results.csv"
+        check("non-run command passes", run(ev("ls -la", w))[0] == 0)
+        check("malformed input passes", run({}, raw="not json")[0] == 0)
+        check("no earlier results passes", run(ev(cmd, os.path.join(tmp, "empty")))[0] == 0)
+        check("repeat of latest batch passes", run(ev("asb run round_1.csv --output round_1_results.csv", w, "r"))[0] == 0)
+        code, err = run(ev(cmd, w))
+        check("first run after a round blocks", code == 2)
+        check("message has numbers and ledger request", "top-10%" in err and "Ledger" in err and "big: 1.9" in err)
+        check("retry in the same state passes", run(ev(cmd, w))[0] == 0)
+        check("other session blocks again", run(ev(cmd, w, "s2"))[0] == 2)
+        check("missing session id never blocks", run(ev(cmd, w, ""))[0] == 0)
+        with open(os.path.join(w, "round_2_results.csv"), "w") as fh:
+            fh.write("item,score\nred_medium,2.2\nblue_medium,1.0\n")
+        cmd3 = "cd %s && asb run round_3.csv --output round_3_results.csv" % w
+        check("new round count blocks again", run(ev(cmd3, tmp))[0] == 2)
+        check("and then passes on retry", run(ev(cmd3, tmp))[0] == 0)
+        # opaque ids joined with a catalog under data/
+        w2 = os.path.join(tmp, "w2")
+        os.makedirs(os.path.join(w2, "data"))

+            fh.write("well_id,fa,fb\na1,L1,B1\na2,L2,B1\na3,L1,B2\na4,L2,B2\n")
+        with open(os.path.join(w2, "round_1_results.csv"), "w") as fh:
+            fh.write("well_id,score\na1,80\na2,10\na3,60\na4,5\n")

+    except Exception:

files.instructions.md:
# Campaign workflow notes

These apply to tasks of the form: seed data, a few irreversible batched `asb run` rounds, then a self-contained
deterministic `final_model.js` that must pass both a discovery gate (hits among your ordered items) and a
held-out ranking (NDCG) gate. Two gates means neither can be left to the end.

## Before round 1
- Read the campaign description (`asb campaign`), the data README, and the model format spec plus the template
  script in full.
- Write a baseline model from the seed data and run the deliver command in its free validation-only mode.
  Re-validate after every round, so a valid model always exists well before the deadline.
- Note both pass criteria and how relevance, ties and the discount are defined; reproduce the metric locally.

## Each round
- Accepted rounds are final; rejected requests are free. Before `asb run`, check the file:
  `python3 /opt/rsi-harness/tools/campaign_check.py batch round_N.csv --size <N> --id-column <name> --previous round_*_results.csv [--catalog <catalog csv>]`
  Fix anything it reports (header, size, duplicates, items already ordered, ids not in the catalog).
- Split each round between the model's top picks and covering groups or levels that are under-sampled so far.
  Track the running count of hits against the discovery threshold and shift toward exploitation when behind.
  This is guidance, not fixed percentages.
- Measurements are noisy; do not read much into a single value that sits near the threshold.

## Using the seed data
- Use the seed data for how the levels of each categorical factor behave, not as a shortlist: the target regime can
  differ from the seed regime. Where targets are defined per group, normalise within group and do not let a global
  score favour easy groups over hard ones.

## Choosing and checking the model
- Pick the final model by cross-validation that mimics the held-out distribution (group the folds by the grouping variable
  that distinguishes held-out items, e.g. a categorical key), with the official metric computed locally:
  `python3 /opt/rsi-harness/tools/campaign_check.py ndcg preds.csv --pred <col> --rel <col> --k <k> [--group <col>] [--threshold <t>]`
  Pass relevance already defined as the task states (clipped/normalised). The tool breaks score ties by input row order;
  prefer models that rarely produce ties.
- The model must be self-contained, deterministic, finite for every input and independent per input; handle levels
  unseen in training with a fallback. Before delivering, run
  `python3 /opt/rsi-harness/tools/campaign_check.py probe <your model file> --inputs-file samples.txt`
  with a few real-format inputs (taken from the catalog), then the validation-only deliver, then the real deliver.
- `python3 /opt/rsi-harness/tools/campaign_check.py selftest` checks the tool itself. The tool is advisory only.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One-shot stop hook: after a campaign model was delivered and time remains, ask for a held-out audit.

Reads the stop event JSON on stdin. Exit 0 lets the agent stop. Exit 2 blocks the stop once and feeds the
audit request (stderr) back to the agent. It never blocks twice per session, never blocks when the event says
a stop hook is already active, and never blocks outside a delivered-campaign context.
Stdlib only. Run with --selftest for a built-in check using temporary fixtures.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone

MARKER_ENV = "RSI_AUDIT_MARKER_DIR"
BUDGET_ENV = "RSI_AUDIT_BUDGET_S"
DEFAULT_BUDGET_S = 28800
MIN_REMAINING_S = 1800
DELIVERED = "deliverable accepted"
MODEL_NAME = "final_model.js"

MESSAGE = """Before stopping: a model has been delivered and time remains. The latest submission is the one scored, so
re-delivery is allowed. Spend a short audit on the held-out ranking gate. Everything you measured so far was
chosen by your own model, so a score over your own picks is biased upward.

1. Build a held-out stand-in. Use the broad first round (or the least model-selected measurements), or hold out whole
   groups of the ordered items (group the folds by the key that distinguishes held-out items). Fit on the rest, keeping
   the seed data in. Score with the official relevance transform exactly as the task states it:
   python3 /opt/rsi-harness/tools/campaign_check.py ndcg preds.csv --pred <col> --rel <col> --k <k> [--group <col>]
2. Compare the delivered model with at least one structurally different alternative on that same stand-in: a
   lower-dimensional or smoother model (fewer features, stronger shrinkage, log or clipped target), and the same
   model with versus without the seed data. Run long fits in the background (nohup ... &) and poll the log, because
   a single command is cut off after about two minutes.
3. Re-deliver only if an alternative beats the delivered model by a clear margin (state it, e.g. at least 0.05 NDCG)
   and the gap is not one or two items. Then: cp final_model.js final_model.prev.js, write the new file,
   python3 /opt/rsi-harness/tools/campaign_check.py probe <model> --inputs-file samples.txt,
   asb deliver <model> --validate-only, and only then the real deliver.
   If nothing wins by the margin, keep the current model: do not re-deliver, and report the stand-in scores.
This audit happens once; state the numbers you compared in the final message."""


def parse_ts(value):
    try:
        if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            return float(value) / (1000.0 if value > 1e11 else 1.0)
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(str(value).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if dt.tzinfo is None:
            dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        return dt.timestamp()
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return None


def read_transcript(path):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            return fh.read()
    except OSError:
        return None


def first_timestamp(text):
    for line in text.splitlines()[:50]:
        m = re.search(r'"timestamp"\s*:\s*("[^"]+"|[0-9.]+)', line)
        if m:
            ts = parse_ts(json.loads(m.group(1)))
            if ts:
                return ts
    return None


def model_exists(cwd):
    for d in (cwd, os.getcwd(), "/app"):
        if d and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, MODEL_NAME)):
            return True
    return False


def marker_path(session):
    base = os.environ.get(MARKER_ENV) or os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "rsi_stop_audit")
    safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", session or "nosession")[:80]
    return base, os.path.join(base, safe + ".done")


def decide(event):
    """Return True if the stop should be blocked for the audit."""
    if event.get("stop_hook_active"):
        return False
    cwd = event.get("cwd") or ""
    text = None
    tp = event.get("transcript_path")
    if tp:
        text = read_transcript(tp)
    if text is not None:
        if DELIVERED not in text or MODEL_NAME not in text:
            return False
        start = first_timestamp(text)
        if start is not None:
            try:
                budget = float(os.environ.get(BUDGET_ENV, DEFAULT_BUDGET_S))
            except ValueError:
                budget = DEFAULT_BUDGET_S
            if time.time() - start > budget - MIN_REMAINING_S:
                return False
    elif not model_exists(cwd):
        return False
    return True


def main():
    if "--selftest" in sys.argv:
        return selftest()
    try:
        event = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
        if not isinstance(event, dict):
            return 0
    except ValueError:
        return 0
    try:
        if not decide(event):
            return 0
        base, marker = marker_path(str(event.get("session_id") or ""))
        if os.path.exists(marker):
            return 0
        os.makedirs(base, exist_ok=True)
        with open(marker, "w") as fh:
            fh.write(str(time.time()))
    except OSError:
        return 0
    sys.stderr.write(MESSAGE + "\n")
    return 2


def selftest():
    import subprocess
    import shutil
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="stopaudit_")
    fails = []
    try:
        env = dict(os.environ, **{MARKER_ENV: os.path.join(tmp, "m")})

        def run(event):
            p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.abspath(__file__)], input=json.dumps(event),
                               capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=30)
            return p.returncode

        def check(name, cond):
            print("%s %s" % ("ok  " if cond else "FAIL", name))
            if not cond:
                fails.append(name)

        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        good = os.path.join(tmp, "good.jsonl")
        with open(good, "w") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps({"timestamp": now, "text": "asb deliver final_model.js"}) + "\n")
            fh.write(json.dumps({"text": "local validation passed\n" + DELIVERED + " (submission 1)"}) + "\n")
        undelivered = os.path.join(tmp, "undelivered.jsonl")
        with open(undelivered, "w") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps({"timestamp": now, "text": "writing final_model.js"}) + "\n")
        late = os.path.join(tmp, "late.jsonl")
        with open(late, "w") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps({"timestamp": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z", "text": "final_model.js " + DELIVERED}) + "\n")
        check("active stop hook never blocks", run({"stop_hook_active": True, "transcript_path": good, "session_id": "a"}) == 0)
        check("no delivery in transcript does not block", run({"transcript_path": undelivered, "session_id": "b"}) == 0)
        check("out of time does not block", run({"transcript_path": late, "session_id": "c"}) == 0)
        check("garbage input does not block", subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.abspath(__file__)], input="not json",
                                                            capture_output=True, text=True, env=env).returncode == 0)
        check("delivered with time left blocks once", run({"transcript_path": good, "session_id": "d"}) == 2)
        check("second stop in same session passes", run({"transcript_path": good, "session_id": "d"}) == 0)
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(tmp, "w"))
        open(os.path.join(tmp, "w", MODEL_NAME), "w").close()
        check("no transcript but model file present blocks", run({"cwd": os.path.join(tmp, "w"), "session_id": "f"}) == 2)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    print("selftest %s" % ("FAILED" if fails else "OK"))
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
